title: Identity, transport and authority are different boundaries
summary: Make each destination, operation and scope explicit before forwarding an event.
objectives: Reject a correct identity acting outside its grant.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 security best current practice
sources.basis: IETF OAuth guidance informs the separation of grants and resource access. This toy scope check is not an OAuth implementation.

sections.title: A bridge is not an authority
paragraphs: A transport can carry an event without permission to use it in another workspace. Authenticate the caller, then check destination scope and allowed action independently.
A token or successful login is not proof that every operation is allowed. Keep provider-specific credentials outside records and examples.

sections.title: Check before forwarding
paragraphs: The synthetic grant permits read in workspace A until time 20. Write, workspace B and time 20 are rejected. The test does not contact a provider.
A production adapter also validates the intended audience, rejects replay and handles revocation. Verify these controls independently of transport and successful login.

exercise.instruction: Run the scope exercise with a wrong workspace, wrong action, expired grant and permitted read.
exercise.expected: Only an in-scope read before expiry succeeds.

limitations: Synthetic comparison only; OAuth, Matrix and provider integrations are not implemented here.
Validate the complete authentication and authorization flow separately before operational use.
